arguments.content:
# Design Specification & Content Outline
# Global CO₂ Emissions: Trends, Regional Shifts, and Per Capita Inequalities

---

## I. Project Information

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Project Name** | co2_emissions_deck |
| **Canvas Format** | PPT 16:9 |
| **Page Count** | 9 slides |
| **Style** | C) Top Consulting (conclusion-first, SCQA framework, pyramid principle) |
| **Target Audience** | Policy analysts and climate negotiators |
| **Usage Occasion** | Policy briefing / climate negotiation preparation |
| **Core Message** | Global CO₂ emissions exceed 35 Bt and have not peaked; the geographic center has shifted to Asia; per capita inequalities remain extreme at 150×; energy policy — not just prosperity — determines outcomes |
| **Date** | April 2026 |
| **Template** | Exhibit Style |

---

## II. Canvas Specification

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| **Format** | Standard 16:9 |
| **Dimensions** | 1280 × 720 px |
| **viewBox** | `0 0 1280 720` |
| **Page Margins** | Left/Right 40px, Top 20px, Bottom 40px |
| **Safe Area** | x: 40–1240, y: 40–680 |
| **Header Area** | y=20, h=60px |
| **Content Area** | y=100, h=520px |
| **Footer Area** | y=660, h=60px |

---

## III. Visual Theme

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| **Style** | Premium dark exhibit with data-forward white content pages |
| **Theme Mode** | Dark covers/chapters + white content pages |
| **Tone** | Authoritative, analytical, data-driven |

### Color Scheme

| Role | HEX | Usage |
|---|---|---|
| **Dark Background** | `#0D1117` | Cover, ending pages |
| **Content White** | `#FFFFFF` | Content page backgrounds |
| **Gradient Blue** | `#1E40AF` | Top bar gradient start |
| **Gradient Purple** | `#7C3AED` | Top bar gradient end |
| **Gold Accent** | `#D4AF37` | Decorative lines, exhibit bar |
| **Purple-Blue** | `#6366F1` | Chapter numbers, accents |
| **Takeaway Bar** | `#111827` | Dark exhibit key-message bar |
| **Body Text** | `#111827` | Primary body on white pages |
| **Secondary Text** | `#4B5563` | Supporting text |
| **Caption Text** | `#9CA3AF` | Footer, captions |
| **Data Red** | `#DC2626` | Rising emitters, alerts |
| **Data Blue** | `#2563EB` | Declining emitters |
| **Data Green** | `#16A34A` | Positive outcomes |
| **Data Orange** | `#EA580C` | Moderate increases |
| **Bar Highlight** | `#1E40AF` | Featured bar in horizontal bar chart |
| **Card Background** | `#F3F4F6` | Light gray stat cards |

---

## IV. Typography System

**Font Stack**: `Arial, "Helvetica Neue", sans-serif`
**Preset**: P5 (English-primary)

| Level | Usage | Size | Weight |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Cover main title | 52px | Bold |
| H2 | Page main title (content pages) | 26px | Bold |
| H3 | Section / exhibit takeaway | 18px | Bold |
| H4 | Card title / label | 16px | Bold |
| P (body) | Body text baseline | 15px | Regular |
| Small | Annotations / captions | 12px | Regular |
| Large KPI | Hero statistics | 64px | Bold |
| Mid KPI | Secondary stats | 36px | Bold |

---

## V. Layout Principles

### Page Zones
- **Top gradient bar**: y=0, h=5px, full-width `#1E40AF`→`#7C3AED`
- **Header / exhibit bar**: y=20–90px (dark `#111827` bg with gold left decoration on content pages)
- **Content area**: y=100–660px
- **Footer**: y=660–720px (`#F9FAFB` strip, source attribution + page number)

### Layout Modes Used
| Mode | Pages |
|---|---|
| Single-column centered (dark hero) | Cover, Ending |
| Exhibit bar + full-width content | Slides 2, 7 |
| Exhibit bar + left-right split (image right) | Slides 3, 4 |
| Exhibit bar + horizontal bar chart | Slide 6 |
| Exhibit bar + stacked comparison visual | Slide 5 |
| Exhibit bar + table + callout | Slide 8 |
| Exhibit bar + numbered bullet list | Slide 9 |

---

## VI. Icon Usage Spec

**Source**: Built-in icon library (640+ icons)
**Placeholder syntax**: `{{ICON:icon_name}}`

### Approved Icon Inventory

| Icon Name | Usage |
|---|---|
| `globe` | Global/world references |
| `factory` | Industrial emissions |
| `chart-line` | Trend / trajectory |
| `chart-bar` | Comparisons |
| `arrow-trend-up` | Rising emissions |
| `arrow-trend-down` | Declining emissions |
| `leaf` | Renewables / environment |
| `bolt` | Energy |
| `fire` | Fossil fuels |
| `cloud` | Atmosphere |
| `flag` | Country references |
| `users` | Per capita / population |
| `circle-exclamation` | Alert / milestone |
| `sun` | Solar energy |
| `wind` | Wind energy |
| `triangle-exclamation` | Warning callout |

---

## VII. Chart Reference List

| Chart Type | Template Path | Used In | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kpi_cards` | templates/charts/kpi_cards.svg | Slide 2 | 429 ppm + 280 ppm baseline callout cards |
| `line_chart` | templates/charts/line_chart.svg | Slide 3 | CO₂ emissions trajectory 1750–2024 |
| `horizontal_bar_chart` | templates/charts/horizontal_bar_chart.svg | Slide 6 | Per capita emissions ranking |
| `stacked_bar_chart` | templates/charts/stacked_bar_chart.svg | Slide 5 | Regional share: 1900 vs 2024 side-by-side |
| `bar_chart` | templates/charts/bar_chart.svg | Slide 4 | Country total emissions comparison |

---

## VIII. Image Resource List

| Filename | Dimensions | Ratio | Layout Suggestion | Purpose | Type | Status | Generation Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| figure_1.jpg | 1384×931 | 1.49 | Standard landscape (left-right split) | Per capita CO₂ over time (historical line chart) — Slide 6 right panel | Diagram | Existing | — |
| figure_3.jpg | 1382×895 | 1.54 | Wide landscape (top-bottom or right panel) | Annual CO₂ by country stacked — Slide 4 right panel | Diagram | Existing | — |
| figure_4.jpg | 1387×918 | 1.51 | Wide landscape (full panel embed) | 2024 annual % change map — Slide 7 main visual | Diagram | Existing | — |

> Note: figure_2.jpg (global trajectory chart) is referenced in the brief but not provided. Slide 3 will use an SVG-drawn line chart built from tabular data in source_brief.md.

---

## IX. Content Outline

### Slide 1 — Cover
**Layout**: Single-column centered, dark background
**Title**: Global CO₂ Emissions: Trends, Regional Shifts, and Per Capita Inequalities
**Subtitle**: A data-driven analysis of global carbon dioxide from the Industrial Revolution to 2024
**Supporting text**: Global Carbon Budget 2025 | NASA Mauna Loa Observatory | Our World in Data
**Scope callout**: 1750 – 2024
**Bottom**: Policy Briefing · April 2026
**Visual elements**: Blue-purple top gradient bar; gold left accent line; light dot-grid decoration; dark `#0D1117` background

---

### Slide 2 — Atmospheric CO₂ Reaches 429 ppm — 50% Above Pre-Industrial Levels
**Layout**: Exhibit bar + two large KPI stat cards + annotation timeline
**Exhibit takeaway**: "At 429 ppm, atmospheric CO₂ is now more than 50% above pre-industrial levels — a change that took thousands of years naturally now occurring in roughly two centuries."
**Left KPI card (large)**: 429 ppm · "Current CO₂ concentration (Feb 2026, Mauna Loa)"
**Right KPI card**: 280 ppm · "Pre-industrial baseline (~1750)"
**Center callout box**: "+53% increase since the Industrial Revolution"
**Below cards — three annotation bullets**:
  - "At least 1.5× greater than the natural increase at the end of the last ice age 20,000 years ago"
  - "The last ice age transition took thousands of years; this increase has occurred in ~200 years"
  - "Continuous monitoring since 1958 at NOAA's Mauna Loa Observatory (the Keeling Curve)"
**Data source footer**: Source: NOAA Mauna Loa Observatory, February 2026

---

### Slide 3 — Global Fossil Fuel CO₂ Emissions Grew Six-Fold: 6 Billion to 35+ Billion Tonnes
**Layout**: Exhibit bar + SVG line chart (left 55%) + three milestone callout cards (right 45%)
**Exhibit takeaway**: "Global emissions have grown more than six-fold since 1950 — from 6 Bt to 35+ Bt today — and have not yet peaked."
**SVG Line Chart** (hand-drawn in SVG, approximate shape):
  - X-axis: 1750, 1800, 1850, 1900, 1950, 1975, 2000, 2024
  - Y-axis: 0 to 40 Bt
  - Shape: Near-flat through 1900, gentle rise to 1950, steep accelerating curve to 2024
  - Key annotation points marked on curve: 1950 (6 Bt), 1990 (20 Bt), 2024 (35+ Bt)
  - Color: `#1E40AF` line on white
**Right milestone cards** (3 stacked):
  - Card 1: "1950 — 6 Bt" (slate)
  - Card 2: "1990 — ~20 Bt" (medium blue)
  - Card 3: "2024 — 35+ Bt" (dark red, bold)
**Data source footer**: Source: Global Carbon Budget 2025; Our World in Data

---

### Slide 4 — China Now Emits Over 12 Billion Tonnes — More Than Double the United States
**Layout**: Exhibit bar + vertical bar chart (left 50%) + embedded figure_3.jpg (right 50%)
**Exhibit takeaway**: "China alone accounts for ~27% of global CO₂ emissions — more than double the US. India has surpassed the EU-27 and is still rising."
**SVG bar chart** (vertical, 7 countries):
  - China: ~12.5 Bt (`#DC2626`, tallest)
  - United States: ~5.0 Bt (`#1E40AF`)
  - India: ~3.0 Bt (`#EA580C`, with upward arrow annotation)
  - EU-27: ~2.7 Bt (`#4B5563`)
  - Germany: ~0.6 Bt (`#4B5563`)
  - United Kingdom: ~0.3 Bt (`#4B5563`)
  - Brazil: ~0.5 Bt (`#4B5563`)
  - Trend labels: China "~27% of global", US "↓ from ~6 Bt peak in 2005", India "↑ Rising fast"
**Right panel**: Embedded figure_3.jpg with caption "Annual CO₂ emissions by country, 1750–2024"
**Data source footer**: Source: Global Carbon Budget 2025; Our World in Data

---

### Slide 5 — Asia Now Accounts for ~50% of Global Emissions; US + Europe Below One-Third
**Layout**: Exhibit bar + side-by-side stacked bar comparison (two tall bars: 1900 vs 2024)
**Exhibit takeaway**: "The geographic center of emissions has fundamentally shifted: from Europe and North America (>90% in 1900) to Asia (~50% today). Africa and South America each contribute only 3–4%."
**Visual**: Two large vertical stacked bars side by side
  - Left bar label: **1900**
    - Europe + US: >90% (`#1E40AF` dark blue, dominant)
    - Rest of World: <10% (`#9CA3AF` light gray)
  - Right bar label: **2024**
    - Asia: ~50% (`#DC2626` red-orange)
    - US: ~14% (`#1E40AF` blue)
    - Europe: ~7% (`#6366F1` purple)
    - Latin America: ~4% (`#16A34A` green)
    - Africa: ~3% (`#EA580C` orange)
    - Other: ~22% (`#9CA3AF` gray)
**Key callout box** (right of chart): 
  - "Asia (incl. China, India, SE Asia) ≈ 50% of global emissions in 2024"

### Slide 2 — Atmospheric CO₂ Reaches 429 ppm — 50% Above Pre-Industrial Levels
**Layout**: Exhibit bar + two large KPI stat cards + annotation timeline

**Data source footer**: Source: NOAA Mauna Loa Observatory, February 2026

### Slide 3 — Global Fossil Fuel CO₂ Emissions Grew Six-Fold: 6 Billion to 35+ Billion Tonnes
**Layout**: Exhibit bar + SVG line chart (left 55%) + three milestone callout cards (right 45%)
**Exhibit takeaway**: "Global emissions have grown more than six-fold since 1950 — from 6 Bt to 35+ Bt today — and have not yet peaked."

**Right milestone cards** (3 stacked):

  - Card 2: "1990 — ~20 Bt" (medium blue)
  - Card 3: "2024 — 35+ Bt" (dark red, bold)
**Data source footer**: Source: Global Carbon Budget 2025; Our World in Data

### Slide 4 — China Now Emits Over 12 Billion Tonnes — More Than Double the United States
**Layout**: Exhibit bar + vertical bar chart (left 50%) + embedded figure_3.jpg (right 50%)
**Exhibit takeaway**: "China alone accounts for ~27% of global CO₂ emissions — more than double the US. India has surpassed the EU-27 and is still rising."
**SVG bar chart** (vertical, 7 countries):

**Right panel**: Embedded figure_3.jpg with caption "Annual CO₂ emissions by country, 1750–2024"
**Data source footer**: Source: Global Carbon Budget 2025; Our World in Data

### Slide 5 — Asia Now Accounts for ~50% of Global Emissions; US + Europe Below One-Third
**Layout**: Exhibit bar + side-by-side stacked bar comparison (two tall bars: 1900 vs 2024)
**Exhibit takeaway**: "The geographic center of emissions has fundamentally shifted: from Europe and North America (>90% in 1900) to Asia (~50% today). Africa and South America each contribute only 3–4%."
**Visual**: Two large vertical stacked bars side by side
  - Left bar label: **1900**
    - Europe + US: >90% (`#1E40AF` dark blue, dominant)
    - Rest of World: <10% (`#9CA3AF` light gray)
  - Right bar label: **2024**

    - US: ~14% (`#1E40AF` blue)
    - Europe: ~7% (`#6366F1` purple)
    - Latin America: ~4% (`#16A34A` green)
    - Africa: ~3% (`#EA580C` orange)

  - "Europe + US combined: <33%"
  - "Africa + South America: only 3–4% each"
**Population context note**: "Asia is home to ~60% of the world's population"
**Data source footer**: Source: Global Carbon Budget 2025; Our World in Data

### Slide 6 — Per Capita Gap: 15 t in the US vs. 0.1 t in Chad — a 150× Disparity
**Layout**: Exhibit bar + horizontal bar chart (left 52%) + figure_1.jpg embedded (right 48%)
**Exhibit takeaway**: "The average American emits in under two days what the average person in Chad emits in an entire year — a 150-fold disparity that defines the equity dimension of climate negotiations."
**Horizontal bar chart** (8 countries, sorted descending):
  - United States: 15 t (`#DC2626`, longest bar)
  - Canada: 13 t (`#DC2626`)
  - China: 9 t (`#EA580C`)
  - EU-27: 7 t (`#4B5563`)
  - World average: 5 t (`#6366F1`, dashed reference line)
  - United Kingdom: 4 t (`#4B5563`)
  - India: 2 t (`#16A34A`)
  - Kenya: <1 t (`#16A34A`)
  - Chad/Niger: 0.1 t (`#16A34A`, shortest bar)
  - World average shown as dashed vertical reference line at 5t
  - "150× gap" callout arrow spanning US bar to Chad bar
**Right panel**: figure_1.jpg embedded with caption "Per capita CO₂ emissions over time"
**Data source footer**: Source: Global Carbon Budget 2025; Our World in Data

### Slide 7 — 2024 Snapshot: US and Europe Cut Emissions While Russia and SE Asia Increase
**Layout**: Exhibit bar + full-width figure_4.jpg (below exhibit bar) + legend strip
**Exhibit takeaway**: "The 2024 emissions map shows a diverging world: the US and most of Europe are cutting (−1% to −5%), while Russia, Southeast Asia, and parts of Africa are increasing (+2% to +10% or more)."
**Main visual**: figure_4.jpg embedded full-width (or near full-width) below exhibit bar
**Below-image legend row** (color-coded):
  - Deep blue: "−5% or more (US, much of Europe)"

  - Orange: "+2% to +5% (Russia, parts of Africa)"
  - Red: "+5% to +10%+ (parts of SE Asia, South America)"

  - "US & EU: −1% to −5%" (blue box)
  - "Russia, SE Asia: +2% to +10%+" (red box)
**Data source footer**: Source: Global Carbon Budget 2025; Our World in Data

### Slide 8 — Energy Mix Explains Why France Emits Far Less Per Capita Than Germany
**Layout**: Exhibit bar + left explanation panel + right comparison table
**Exhibit takeaway**: "Countries at similar prosperity levels can have dramatically different per capita emissions. Energy mix — especially the share of nuclear and renewables — is the key differentiator."
**Left panel — two callout cards**:
  - Card A (blue/green): "France & UK: ~4 t/person — high nuclear + renewable share → lower per capita CO₂"
  - Card B (orange): "Germany & Netherlands: ~7–8 t/person — higher fossil fuel reliance → higher per capita CO₂"
**Right panel — comparison table**:

| Country | Per Capita CO₂ | Nuclear Share | Renewable Share | Fossil Reliance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| France | ~4 t | High | Moderate | Low |
| United Kingdom | ~4 t | Moderate | High | Declining |
| Germany | ~7 t | Phased out | Growing | High (gas/coal) |
| Netherlands | ~8 t | Low | Growing | High (gas) |

**Below table note**: "Policy choices — not just economic development — determine per capita outcomes. This has direct implications for equity-based emission reduction frameworks."
**Data source footer**: Source: Global Carbon Budget 2025; Our World in Data

---

### Slide 9 — Key Takeaways: Emissions Still Rising, But the Map of Responsibility Is Shifting
**Layout**: Exhibit bar + numbered list of 5 takeaways (two-column grid)
**Exhibit takeaway**: "Five facts every climate negotiator needs: emissions are still rising, but who is responsible — historically and per capita — is more nuanced than total tonnage alone."
**Five takeaway cards** (numbered, arranged 3+2 grid):
  1. **35+ Billion Tonnes and Climbing** — "Global annual CO₂ emissions have not yet peaked. The slowing of growth is encouraging, but absolute levels continue to rise."
  2. **China Leads at 27%, India Rising** — "China emits >12.5 Bt (~27% of global total). India (~3 Bt) is the third-largest emitter and growing rapidly."
  3. **150× Per Capita Inequality** — "The US emits ~15 t/person vs. Chad at ~0.1 t/person. Equity-adjusted frameworks must account for this disparity."
  4. **US and Europe Are Declining** — "US and Europe show emissions reductions, but historical cumulative responsibility remains large — a key point in loss-and-damage negotiations."
  5. **Energy Mix Is the Policy Lever** — "Countries at comparable prosperity levels (France vs. Germany) show that policy and energy choices — not just GDP — determine per capita outcomes."
**Bottom source strip**: Source: Global Carbon Budget 2025 | NASA NOAA Mauna Loa Observatory | Our World in Data

# Executor Common Guidelines

> Style-specific content is in the corresponding `executor-{style}.md`. Technical constraints are in shared-standards.md.

---

## 1. Template Adherence Rules

If template files exist in the project's `templates/` directory, the template structure must be followed:

| Page Type | Corresponding Template | Adherence Rules |
|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|
| Cover | `01_cover.svg` | Inherit background, decorative elements, layout structure; replace placeholder content |
| Chapter | `02_chapter.svg` | Inherit numbering style, title position, decorative elements |
| Content | `03_content.svg` | Inherit header/footer styles; **content area may be freely laid out** |
| Ending | `04_ending.svg` | Inherit background, thank-you message position, contact info layout |
| TOC | `02_toc.svg` | **Optional**: Inherit TOC title, list styles |

### Page-Template Mapping Declaration (Required Output)

Before generating each page, you must explicitly output which template (or "free design") is used:

```
📝 **Template mapping**: `templates/01_cover.svg` (or "None (free design)")
🎯 **Adherence rules / layout strategy**: [specific description]
```

- **Content pages**: Templates only define header and footer; the content area is freely laid out by the Executor
- **No template**: Generate entirely per the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 2. Design Parameter Confirmation (Mandatory Step)

> Before generating the first SVG page, you **must review the key design parameters from the Design Specification & Content Outline** to ensure all subsequent generation strictly follows the spec.

Must output confirmation including: canvas dimensions, body font size, color scheme (primary/secondary/accent HEX values), font plan.

**Why is this step mandatory?** Prevents the "spec says one thing, execution does another" disconnect.

---

## 3. Execution Guidelines

- **Proximity principle**: Place related elements close together to form visual groups; increase spacing between unrelated groups to reinforce logical structure
- **Absolute spec adherence**: Strictly follow the color, layout, canvas format, and typography parameters in the spec
- **Follow template structure**: If templates exist, inherit the template's visual framework
- **Phased batch generation** (recommended):
  1. **Visual Construction Phase**: Generate all SVG pages continuously, ensuring high consistency in design style and layout coordinates (Visual Consistency)
  2. **Logic Construction Phase**: After all SVGs are finalized, batch-generate speaker notes to ensure narrative coherence (Narrative Continuity)
- **Technical specifications**: See [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md) for SVG technical constraints and PPT compatibility rules

### SVG File Naming Convention

File naming format: `<number>_<page_name>.svg`

- **Chinese content** → Chinese naming: `01_封面.svg`, `02_目录.svg`, `03_核心优势.svg`
- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01
- **Page name**: Concise and descriptive, matching the page title in the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 4. Icon Usage

Four approaches: **A: Emoji** (`<text>🚀</text>`) | **B: AI-generated** (SVG basic shapes) | **C: Built-in library** (`templates/icons/` 640+ icons, recommended) | **D: Custom** (user-specified)

**Built-in icons — Placeholder method (recommended)**:

```xml
<use data-icon="chart-bar" x="100" y="200" width="48" height="48" fill="#005587"/>
```

> No need to manually run `embed_icons.py`; `finalize_svg.py` post-processing tool will auto-embed icons.

**Common icons**: `chart-bar` `arrow-trend-up` `users` `cog` `circle-checkmark` `target` `clock` `file` `dollar` `lightbulb`

> ⚠️ **Icon validation rule**: If the Design Specification includes an icon inventory list, Executor may **only** use icons from that approved list. Using icon names not in the index is FORBIDDEN — verify against `templates/icons/icons_index.json` if uncertain.

Full index: `templates/icons/README.md`

---

## 5. Chart Reference

When the Design Spec includes a **VII. Chart Reference List**, read the referenced SVG templates from `templates/charts/` to understand common chart patterns.

**Adaptation rules**:
- **Must preserve**: Chart type (bar/line/pie etc.) as specified in the Design Spec
- **Must adapt**: Data values, labels, colors (match the project's color scheme), and dimensions to fit the page layout
- **May adjust**: Axis ranges, grid lines, legend position, spacing — as long as the chart remains accurate and readable
- **Must NOT**: Change chart type without Design Spec justification, or remove data points specified in the outline

> Chart templates: `templates/charts/` (33 types). Index: `templates/charts/charts_index.json`

---

## 6. Image Handling

Handle images based on their status in the Design Specification's "Image Resource List":

| Status | Source | Handling |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |

**Reference**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" ... preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`

**Placeholder**: Dashed border `<rect stroke-dasharray="8,4" .../>` + description text

---

## 7. Font Usage

Apply corresponding fonts for different text roles based on the font plan in the Design Specification & Content Outline:

| Role | Chinese Recommended | English Recommended |
|------|--------------------|--------------------|
| Title font | Microsoft YaHei / KaiTi / SimHei | Arial / Georgia |
| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |
| Emphasis font | SimHei | Arial Black / Consolas |
| Annotation font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Arial / Times |

---

## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework

### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document

After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.

**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.

**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.

**Basic stage direction markers** (common to all styles):

| Marker | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |

> Each style may extend with additional markers (`[Interactive]`/`[Data]`/`[Scan Room]`/`[Benchmark]` etc.), see `executor-{style}.md`.

**Requirements**:

- Notes should be conversational and flow naturally
- Highlight each page's core information and presentation key points
- Users can manually edit and override in the `notes/` directory

### Task 2. Split Into Per-Page Note Files

Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.

**File naming convention**:

- **Recommended**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
- **Compatible**: Also supports `slide01.md` format (backward compatibility)

---

## 9. Next Steps After Completion

> **Auto-continuation**: After Visual Construction Phase (all SVG pages) and Logic Construction Phase (all notes) are complete, the Executor proceeds directly to the post-processing pipeline.

**Post-processing & Export** (see [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md)):

```bash
# 1. Split speaker notes
python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>

# 2. SVG post-processing (auto-embed icons, images, etc.)
python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>

# 3. Export PPTX
python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
```

# Executor Common Guidelines

> Style-specific content is in the corresponding `executor-{style}.md`. Technical constraints are in shared-standards.md.

---

## 1. Template Adherence Rules

If template files exist in the project's `templates/` directory, the template structure must be followed:

| Page Type | Corresponding Template | Adherence Rules |
|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|
| Cover | `01_cover.svg` | Inherit background, decorative elements, layout structure; replace placeholder content |
| Chapter | `02_chapter.svg` | Inherit numbering style, title position, decorative elements |
| Content | `03_content.svg` | Inherit header/footer styles; **content area may be freely laid out** |
| Ending | `04_ending.svg` | Inherit background, thank-you message position, contact info layout |
| TOC | `02_toc.svg` | **Optional**: Inherit TOC title, list styles |

### Page-Template Mapping Declaration (Required Output)

Before generating each page, you must explicitly output which template (or "free design") is used:

```
📝 **Template mapping**: `templates/01_cover.svg` (or "None (free design)")
🎯 **Adherence rules / layout strategy**: [specific description]
```

- **Content pages**: Templates only define header and footer; the content area is freely laid out by the Executor
- **No template**: Generate entirely per the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 2. Design Parameter Confirmation (Mandatory Step)

> Before generating the first SVG page, you **must review the key design parameters from the Design Specification & Content Outline** to ensure all subsequent generation strictly follows the spec.

Must output confirmation including: canvas dimensions, body font size, color scheme (primary/secondary/accent HEX values), font plan.

**Why is this step mandatory?** Prevents the "spec says one thing, execution does another" disconnect.

---

## 3. Execution Guidelines

- **Proximity principle**: Place related elements close together to form visual groups; increase spacing between unrelated groups to reinforce logical structure
- **Absolute spec adherence**: Strictly follow the color, layout, canvas format, and typography parameters in the spec
- **Follow template structure**: If templates exist, inherit the template's visual framework
- **Phased batch generation** (recommended):
  1. **Visual Construction Phase**: Generate all SVG pages continuously, ensuring high consistency in design style and layout coordinates (Visual Consistency)
  2. **Logic Construction Phase**: After all SVGs are finalized, batch-generate speaker notes to ensure narrative coherence (Narrative Continuity)
- **Technical specifications**: See [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md) for SVG technical constraints and PPT compatibility rules

### SVG File Naming Convention

File naming format: `<number>_<page_name>.svg`

- **Chinese content** → Chinese naming: `01_封面.svg`, `02_目录.svg`, `03_核心优势.svg`
- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01
- **Page name**: Concise and descriptive, matching the page title in the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 4. Icon Usage

Four approaches: **A: Emoji** (`<text>🚀</text>`) | **B: AI-generated** (SVG basic shapes) | **C: Built-in library** (`templates/icons/` 640+ icons, recommended) | **D: Custom** (user-specified)

**Built-in icons — Placeholder method (recommended)**:

```xml
<use data-icon="chart-bar" x="100" y="200" width="48" height="48" fill="#005587"/>
```

> No need to manually run `embed_icons.py`; `finalize_svg.py` post-processing tool will auto-embed icons.

**Common icons**: `chart-bar` `arrow-trend-up` `users` `cog` `circle-checkmark` `target` `clock` `file` `dollar` `lightbulb`

> ⚠️ **Icon validation rule**: If the Design Specification includes an icon inventory list, Executor may **only** use icons from that approved list. Using icon names not in the index is FORBIDDEN — verify against `templates/icons/icons_index.json` if uncertain.

Full index: `templates/icons/README.md`

---

## 5. Chart Reference

When the Design Spec includes a **VII. Chart Reference List**, read the referenced SVG templates from `templates/charts/` to understand common chart patterns.

**Adaptation rules**:
- **Must preserve**: Chart type (bar/line/pie etc.) as specified in the Design Spec
- **Must adapt**: Data values, labels, colors (match the project's color scheme), and dimensions to fit the page layout
- **May adjust**: Axis ranges, grid lines, legend position, spacing — as long as the chart remains accurate and readable
- **Must NOT**: Change chart type without Design Spec justification, or remove data points specified in the outline

> Chart templates: `templates/charts/` (33 types). Index: `templates/charts/charts_index.json`

---

## 6. Image Handling

Handle images based on their status in the Design Specification's "Image Resource List":

| Status | Source | Handling |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |

**Reference**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" ... preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`

**Placeholder**: Dashed border `<rect stroke-dasharray="8,4" .../>` + description text

---

## 7. Font Usage

Apply corresponding fonts for different text roles based on the font plan in the Design Specification & Content Outline:

| Role | Chinese Recommended | English Recommended |
|------|--------------------|--------------------|
| Title font | Microsoft YaHei / KaiTi / SimHei | Arial / Georgia |
| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |
| Emphasis font | SimHei | Arial Black / Consolas |
| Annotation font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Arial / Times |

---

## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework

### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document

After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.

**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.

**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.

**Basic stage direction markers** (common to all styles):

| Marker | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |

> Each style may extend with additional markers (`[Interactive]`/`[Data]`/`[Scan Room]`/`[Benchmark]` etc.), see `executor-{style}.md`.

**Requirements**:

- Notes should be conversational and flow naturally
- Highlight each page's core information and presentation key points
- Users can manually edit and override in the `notes/` directory

### Task 2. Split Into Per-Page Note Files

Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.

**File naming convention**:

- **Recommended**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
- **Compatible**: Also supports `slide01.md` format (backward compatibility)

---

## 9. Next Steps After Completion

> **Auto-continuation**: After Visual Construction Phase (all SVG pages) and Logic Construction Phase (all notes) are complete, the Executor proceeds directly to the post-processing pipeline.

**Post-processing & Export** (see [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md)):

```bash
# 1. Split speaker notes
python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>

# 2. SVG post-processing (auto-embed icons, images, etc.)
python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>

# 3. Export PPTX
python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
```

1	# Executor Consultant Top — Top-tier Consulting Style (MBB Level)
2	
3	> Common guidelines: executor-base.md. Technical constraints: shared-standards.md.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Role Definition
8	
9	An MBB-level (McKinsey / Bain / BCG) top-tier consulting style SVG design executor. Suitable for strategic planning, board presentations, investment roadshows, C-suite decision support, and other **premium consulting** scenarios. Core characteristics: data-driven insights, pyramid-structured narrative, extreme simplicity. Output targets C-level decision-makers.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## SCQA Framework (Narrative Structure)
14	
15	Every MBB-level presentation follows the SCQA narrative structure:
16	
17	| Element | Purpose | Typical Pages |
18	|---------|---------|---------------|
19	| **S - Situation** | Establish shared context | Cover / Pages 1-2 |
20	| **C - Complication** | Introduce the problem / tension | Pages 2-3 |
21	| **Q - Question** | The implicit or explicit question to solve | Transition page |
22	| **A - Answer** | Core solution | All body pages |
23	
24	**Page sequencing**: Cover embodies S+C → Executive Summary answers Q → Chapters develop A → Closing revisits S
25	
26	**Title writing**:
27	
28	| SCQA Element | Weak Title | MBB-level Title |
29	|-------------|------------|-----------------|
30	| S | "Industry Background" | "Digital penetration surpasses 60%, industry enters deep waters" |
31	| C | "Challenges Faced" | "Yet three structural contradictions constrain scaled deployment" |
32	| Q | "Strategic Question" | "How to move from pilot to full deployment within 18 months?" |
33	| A | "Solution" | "Three-phase path: Focus, Expand, Scale" |
34	
35	---
36	
37	## Data Contextualization (Never Present Data in Isolation)
38	
39	> **Golden Rule**: Never display a single data point in isolation. Every number needs context.
40	
41	| Method | Pattern | Visual Implementation |
42	|--------|---------|----------------------|
43	| **Time comparison** | "From X to Y" | Line chart + arrow annotating magnitude of change |
44	| **Benchmark** | "X vs industry average Y" | Bar chart with gray dashed baseline |
45	| **Competitive comparison** | "Us X vs Competitor Y" | Side-by-side bar chart, highlight own data |
46	| **Target gap** | "Actual X / Target Y" | Progress bar + gap annotation |
47	| **Ranking** | "Ranked #N of M" | Horizontal bar chart + highlight marker |
48	
49	**Data annotation three essentials**: Every data visualization must include (1) The value itself (large bold font) (2) Comparison reference (baseline / prior period / competitor) (3) Meaning interpretation ("So what?")
50	
51	```xml
52	<text x="160" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">97.3%</text>
53	<text x="160" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Industry avg 82% | Competitor A 89%</text>
54	<text x="160" y="335" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#059669">Leading industry by 15.3 percentage points</text>
55	```
56	
57	---
58	
59	## Pyramid Principle (Conclusion First)
60	
61	> Executives don't care about your *process* — they care about *results*.
62	
63	```
64	         ┌─────────────────┐
65	         │  Core Conclusion │   ← Page title / Takeaway
66	         └────────┬────────┘
67	      ┌───────────┼───────────┐
68	  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐
69	  │ Arg 1 │  │ Arg 2 │  │ Arg 3 │   ← Key supporting points
70	  └───────┘  └───────┘  └───────┘
71	```
72	
73	| Level | Position | Font Size |
74	|-------|----------|-----------|
75	| Core conclusion | Takeaway Box | 16-18px bold |
76	| Arguments | Content area body | 14-16px |
77	| Supporting data | Charts / cards | 12-14px |
78	
79	**Contrast**: Title "Market Research Results" (wrong) → "Metaverse needs 5-10 years to reach scale" (right); Body "We researched... and found..." (wrong) → "Three arguments: (1)... (2)... (3)..." (right)
80	
81	---
82

# Executor Consultant Top — Top-tier Consulting Style (MBB Level)

> Common guidelines: executor-base.md. Technical constraints: shared-standards.md.

---

## Role Definition

An MBB-level (McKinsey / Bain / BCG) top-tier consulting style SVG design executor. Suitable for strategic planning, board presentations, investment roadshows, C-suite decision support, and other **premium consulting** scenarios. Core characteristics: data-driven insights, pyramid-structured narrative, extreme simplicity. Output targets C-level decision-makers.

---

## SCQA Framework (Narrative Structure)

Every MBB-level presentation follows the SCQA narrative structure:

| Element | Purpose | Typical Pages |
|---------|---------|---------------|
| **S - Situation** | Establish shared context | Cover / Pages 1-2 |
| **C - Complication** | Introduce the problem / tension | Pages 2-3 |
| **Q - Question** | The implicit or explicit question to solve | Transition page |
| **A - Answer** | Core solution | All body pages |

**Page sequencing**: Cover embodies S+C → Executive Summary answers Q → Chapters develop A → Closing revisits S

**Title writing**:

| SCQA Element | Weak Title | MBB-level Title |
|-------------|------------|-----------------|
| S | "Industry Background" | "Digital penetration surpasses 60%, industry enters deep waters" |
| C | "Challenges Faced" | "Yet three structural contradictions constrain scaled deployment" |
| Q | "Strategic Question" | "How to move from pilot to full deployment within 18 months?" |
| A | "Solution" | "Three-phase path: Focus, Expand, Scale" |

---

## Data Contextualization (Never Present Data in Isolation)

> **Golden Rule**: Never display a single data point in isolation. Every number needs context.

| Method | Pattern | Visual Implementation |
|--------|---------|----------------------|
| **Time comparison** | "From X to Y" | Line chart + arrow annotating magnitude of change |
| **Benchmark** | "X vs industry average Y" | Bar chart with gray dashed baseline |
| **Competitive comparison** | "Us X vs Competitor Y" | Side-by-side bar chart, highlight own data |
| **Target gap** | "Actual X / Target Y" | Progress bar + gap annotation |
| **Ranking** | "Ranked #N of M" | Horizontal bar chart + highlight marker |

**Data annotation three essentials**: Every data visualization must include (1) The value itself (large bold font) (2) Comparison reference (baseline / prior period / competitor) (3) Meaning interpretation ("So what?")

```xml
<text x="160" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">97.3%</text>
<text x="160" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Industry avg 82% | Competitor A 89%</text>
<text x="160" y="335" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#059669">Leading industry by 15.3 percentage points</text>
```

---

## Pyramid Principle (Conclusion First)

> Executives don't care about your *process* — they care about *results*.

```
         ┌─────────────────┐
         │  Core Conclusion │   ← Page title / Takeaway
         └────────┬────────┘
      ┌───────────┼───────────┐
  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐
  │ Arg 1 │  │ Arg 2 │  │ Arg 3 │   ← Key supporting points
  └───────┘  └───────┘  └───────┘
```

| Level | Position | Font Size |
|-------|----------|-----------|
| Core conclusion | Takeaway Box | 16-18px bold |
| Arguments | Content area body | 14-16px |
| Supporting data | Charts / cards | 12-14px |

**Contrast**: Title "Market Research Results" (wrong) → "Metaverse needs 5-10 years to reach scale" (right); Body "We researched... and found..." (wrong) → "Three arguments: (1)... (2)... (3)..." (right)

---

## MBB-level Layout Patterns

### Content Page Standard Structure (1280x720)

```
┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│ Gradient top bar (0,0 → 1280,6)  │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Assertion title (x=40, y=50, 24px)│
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Takeaway Box (x=40, y=75,        │  ← Dark background + white text, one-sentence conclusion
│   w=1200, h=45)                  │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Content area (x=40, y=140,       │  ← Charts / data / analysis
│   w=1200, h=520)                 │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Source | CONFIDENTIAL | Page #    │  ← y=700, 10px
└──────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Strategic Roadmap

Three phases laid out horizontally, `<rect rx="8">` + title + action list, `<polygon>` arrows connecting:

```
Focus Core (0-6mo)  ──>  Expand Capability (6-12mo)  ──>  Scale Up (12-18mo)
x=40,w=380              x=450,w=380                     x=860,w=380
```

### Benchmarking Matrix

Horizontal table; own row highlighted in theme color, others in gray. Leading indicators marked green, lagging marked red. Use `<circle>` or `<rect>` to build score points.

### Waterfall Chart (Change Attribution)

Start → increase/decrease factors → End. Positive factors green bars, negative factors red bars, start/end points dark bars, cumulative line as dashed connector.

---

## Strategic Use of Color

MBB-level color usage is extremely restrained — color serves information:

| Purpose | Method |
|---------|--------|
| **Focus** | Target data in theme color, everything else gray |
| **Reduce cognitive load** | Same series differentiated by opacity (`fill-opacity` 1.0/0.6/0.3) |
| **Semantics** | Green = positive, Red = negative, Gray = baseline |
| **Branding** | Gradient top bar / decorative lines in brand color |

**Commandments**: No more than 3 primary colors; accent color used at most 2-3 places globally; data series use same-hue depth variations, not different colors; background white or very light gray.

---

## Chart vs Table Selection Matrix

| Scenario | Recommended Form | Reason |
|----------|-----------------|--------|
| Comparing 2-7 categories | **Bar chart** | Visual comparison is intuitive |
| Time trends | **Line chart** | Time series clarity |
| Precise values / large rankings | **Table** | 50 data points in a bar chart would be chaotic |
| Proportional composition | **Donut chart** | More modern than pie charts |
| Two-dimensional positioning | **2x2 matrix** | Strategic quadrant analysis |
| Change attribution | **Waterfall chart** | Factor decomposition |

---

## Speaker Notes Style

### Narrative Tone

Targeting **executives / decision-makers**. Pyramid structure — every sentence carries information. Composed, authoritative, and insightful tone.

### Stage Direction Markers

| Marker | Purpose | Example |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Silence after key insight, let executives absorb | "This means we are missing a billion-dollar market. [Pause]" |
| `[Scan Room]` | Observe decision-makers' reactions, decide whether to elaborate | "[Scan Room] If there are questions, I can elaborate." |
| `[Data]` | Conversational number delivery | "[Data] 63% → nearly two-thirds" |
| `[Benchmark]` | Emphasize comparison baseline | "[Benchmark] Compared to the industry average of 12%, our 23% is nearly double" |
| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Building on the strategic framework, let's drill into the implementation path." |

### Notes Writing Guidelines

- **Pyramid structure**: Conclusion → Arguments → Details
- **Data contextualization**: Every number has a comparison reference
- **Executive language**: "The strategic implication is...", "The core insight is..."
- **Flex mechanism**: Annotate "content that can be skipped if time is tight" for flexible duration
- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core insight (2) Data support (3) Strategic implication`

### Notes Example

```markdown
# 03_strategic_path

[Transition] Having clarified the problem and the opportunity, now comes the most critical part — our response path.

We recommend a three-phase strategy. [Pause]

Phase one: Focus. Over the next six months, concentrate resources on conquering the Eastern China market.
[Data] Eastern China contributes nearly two-thirds of industry growth, [Benchmark] yet our penetration rate is only half of Competitor A's. [Pause]

Phase two: Expand. Use Eastern China as a template, replicate to Southern and Northern China.
Phase three: Scale. Leverage a digital platform for nationwide coverage.

[Scan Room] The resource allocation for phase one is in the appendix — would you like me to walk through it now?

Key points: (1) Focus-Expand-Scale three-phase approach (2) Data-backed Eastern China priority (3) 18-month full deployment
Duration: 3 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, skip phase two and three details and go straight to financial impact]
```

---

## MBB-level Quality Checklist Supplement

### Content Level

- [ ] **SCQA complete**: Overall follows Situation-Complication-Question-Answer structure
- [ ] **Data contextualized**: Every data point has a comparison reference
- [ ] **Conclusion first**: Every page's Takeaway Box has a one-sentence conclusion
- [ ] **MECE principle**: Categorized analysis is mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive

### Visual Level

- [ ] **Color with intent**: Colors serve information delivery
- [ ] **Ample whitespace**: Not crowded; information can "breathe"
- [ ] **Visual hierarchy**: Conclusion > Arguments > Details, differentiated by font size/weight
- [ ] **Brand consistency**: Gradient top bar and footer unified throughout

### Notes Level

- [ ] **Pyramid structure**: Every page is conclusion-first
- [ ] **Stage markers complete**: [Pause] and [Scan Room] at key positions
- [ ] **Flex content annotated**: Supports flexible duration

# Executor Consultant Top — Top-tier Consulting Style (MBB Level)

> Common guidelines: executor-base.md. Technical constraints: shared-standards.md.

---

## Role Definition

An MBB-level (McKinsey / Bain / BCG) top-tier consulting style SVG design executor. Suitable for strategic planning, board presentations, investment roadshows, C-suite decision support, and other **premium consulting** scenarios. Core characteristics: data-driven insights, pyramid-structured narrative, extreme simplicity. Output targets C-level decision-makers.

---

## SCQA Framework (Narrative Structure)

Every MBB-level presentation follows the SCQA narrative structure:

| Element | Purpose | Typical Pages |
|---------|---------|---------------|
| **S - Situation** | Establish shared context | Cover / Pages 1-2 |
| **C - Complication** | Introduce the problem / tension | Pages 2-3 |
| **Q - Question** | The implicit or explicit question to solve | Transition page |
| **A - Answer** | Core solution | All body pages |

**Page sequencing**: Cover embodies S+C → Executive Summary answers Q → Chapters develop A → Closing revisits S

**Title writing**:

| SCQA Element | Weak Title | MBB-level Title |
|-------------|------------|-----------------|
| S | "Industry Background" | "Digital penetration surpasses 60%, industry enters deep waters" |
| C | "Challenges Faced" | "Yet three structural contradictions constrain scaled deployment" |
| Q | "Strategic Question" | "How to move from pilot to full deployment within 18 months?" |
| A | "Solution" | "Three-phase path: Focus, Expand, Scale" |

---

## Data Contextualization (Never Present Data in Isolation)

> **Golden Rule**: Never display a single data point in isolation. Every number needs context.

| Method | Pattern | Visual Implementation |
|--------|---------|----------------------|
| **Time comparison** | "From X to Y" | Line chart + arrow annotating magnitude of change |
| **Benchmark** | "X vs industry average Y" | Bar chart with gray dashed baseline |
| **Competitive comparison** | "Us X vs Competitor Y" | Side-by-side bar chart, highlight own data |
| **Target gap** | "Actual X / Target Y" | Progress bar + gap annotation |
| **Ranking** | "Ranked #N of M" | Horizontal bar chart + highlight marker |

**Data annotation three essentials**: Every data visualization must include (1) The value itself (large bold font) (2) Comparison reference (baseline / prior period / competitor) (3) Meaning interpretation ("So what?")

```xml
<text x="160" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">97.3%</text>
<text x="160" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Industry avg 82% | Competitor A 89%</text>
<text x="160" y="335" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#059669">Leading industry by 15.3 percentage points</text>
```

---

## Pyramid Principle (Conclusion First)

> Executives don't care about your *process* — they care about *results*.

```
         ┌─────────────────┐
         │  Core Conclusion │   ← Page title / Takeaway
         └────────┬────────┘
      ┌───────────┼───────────┐
  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐
  │ Arg 1 │  │ Arg 2 │  │ Arg 3 │   ← Key supporting points
  └───────┘  └───────┘  └───────┘
```

| Level | Position | Font Size |
|-------|----------|-----------|
| Core conclusion | Takeaway Box | 16-18px bold |
| Arguments | Content area body | 14-16px |
| Supporting data | Charts / cards | 12-14px |

**Contrast**: Title "Market Research Results" (wrong) → "Metaverse needs 5-10 years to reach scale" (right); Body "We researched... and found..." (wrong) → "Three arguments: (1)... (2)... (3)..." (right)

---

## MBB-level Layout Patterns

### Content Page Standard Structure (1280x720)

```
┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│ Gradient top bar (0,0 → 1280,6)  │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Assertion title (x=40, y=50, 24px)│

Three phases laid out horizontally, `<rect rx="8">` + title + action list, `<polygon>` arrows connecting:

```
Focus Core (0-6mo)  ──>  Expand Capability (6-12mo)  ──>  Scale Up (12-18mo)

```

### Waterfall Chart (Change Attribution)

---

| Purpose | Method |

### Narrative Tone

Targeting **executives / decision-makers**. Pyramid structure — every sentence carries information. Composed, authoritative, and insightful tone.

### Stage Direction Markers

| Marker | Purpose | Example |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Silence after key insight, let executives absorb | "This means we are missing a billion-dollar market. [Pause]" |
| `[Scan Room]` | Observe decision-makers' reactions, decide whether to elaborate | "[Scan Room] If there are questions, I can elaborate." |
| `[Data]` | Conversational number delivery | "[Data] 63% → nearly two-thirds" |
| `[Benchmark]` | Emphasize comparison baseline | "[Benchmark] Compared to the industry average of 12%, our 23% is nearly double" |
| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Building on the strategic framework, let's drill into the implementation path." |

### Notes Writing Guidelines

- **Pyramid structure**: Conclusion → Arguments → Details
- **Data contextualization**: Every number has a comparison reference
- **Executive language**: "The strategic implication is...", "The core insight is..."
- **Flex mechanism**: Annotate "content that can be skipped if time is tight" for flexible duration
- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core insight (2) Data support (3) Strategic implication`

### Notes Example

```markdown
# 03_strategic_path

[Transition] Having clarified the problem and the opportunity, now comes the most critical part — our response path.

We recommend a three-phase strategy. [Pause]

Phase one: Focus. Over the next six months, concentrate resources on conquering the Eastern China market.
[Data] Eastern China contributes nearly two-thirds of industry growth, [Benchmark] yet our penetration rate is only half of Competitor A's. [Pause]

Phase two: Expand. Use Eastern China as a template, replicate to Southern and Northern China.
Phase three: Scale. Leverage a digital platform for nationwide coverage.

[Scan Room] The resource allocation for phase one is in the appendix — would you like me to walk through it now?

Key points: (1) Focus-Expand-Scale three-phase approach (2) Data-backed Eastern China priority (3) 18-month full deployment
Duration: 3 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, skip phase two and three details and go straight to financial impact]
```

---

## MBB-level Quality Checklist Supplement

### Content Level

- [ ] **SCQA complete**: Overall follows Situation-Complication-Question-Answer structure
- [ ] **Data contextualized**: Every data point has a comparison reference
- [ ] **Conclusion first**: Every page's Takeaway Box has a one-sentence conclusion
- [ ] **MECE principle**: Categorized analysis is mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive

### Visual Level

- [ ] **Color with intent**: Colors serve information delivery
- [ ] **Ample whitespace**: Not crowded; information can "breathe"
- [ ] **Visual hierarchy**: Conclusion > Arguments > Details, differentiated by font size/weight
- [ ] **Brand consistency**: Gradient top bar and footer unified throughout

### Notes Level

- [ ] **Pyramid structure**: Every page is conclusion-first
- [ ] **Stage markers complete**: [Pause] and [Scan Room] at key positions
- [ ] **Flex content annotated**: Supports flexible duration

arguments.content:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720" width="1280" height="720">
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="topBar" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#1E40AF"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#7C3AED"/>
    </linearGradient>
  </defs>

  <!-- White background -->
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>

  <!-- Top gradient bar -->
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="5" fill="url(#topBar)"/>

  <!-- Page title -->
  <text x="40" y="46" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#111827">Atmospheric CO₂ Reaches 429 ppm — 50% Above Pre-Industrial Levels</text>

  <!-- Exhibit takeaway bar -->
  <rect x="40" y="58" width="1200" height="50" rx="2" fill="#111827"/>
  <rect x="40" y="58" width="4" height="50" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <text x="56" y="80" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">At 429 ppm, atmospheric CO₂ is now more than 50% above pre-industrial levels — a change that took thousands of years</text>
  <text x="56" y="98" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">naturally but has occurred in roughly two centuries.</text>

  <!-- LEFT: Large KPI card — current -->
  <rect x="40" y="122" width="360" height="190" rx="8" fill="#F3F4F6"/>
  <rect x="40" y="122" width="360" height="5" rx="2" fill="#DC2626"/>
  <text x="220" y="170" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="68" font-weight="bold" fill="#DC2626">429</text>
  <text x="220" y="198" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#DC2626">ppm</text>
  <text x="220" y="224" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#4B5563">Current CO₂ concentration</text>
  <text x="220" y="240" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#4B5563">Feb 2026 — NOAA Mauna Loa Observatory</text>
  <text x="220" y="302" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#9CA3AF">Highest in at least 800,000 years of ice core records</text>

  <!-- MIDDLE: Percentage increase callout -->
  <rect x="420" y="122" width="220" height="190" rx="8" fill="#1E40AF"/>
  <text x="530" y="180" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="52" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">+53%</text>
  <text x="530" y="214" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#BFDBFE">increase since</text>
  <text x="530" y="232" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#BFDBFE">Industrial Revolution</text>
  <text x="530" y="260" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#93C5FD">280 ppm → 429 ppm</text>
  <text x="530" y="300" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#93C5FD">≈ 2 centuries</text>

  <!-- RIGHT: Baseline KPI card -->
  <rect x="660" y="122" width="360" height="190" rx="8" fill="#F3F4F6"/>
  <rect x="660" y="122" width="360" height="5" rx="2" fill="#4B5563"/>
  <text x="840" y="170" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="68" font-weight="bold" fill="#4B5563">280</text>
  <text x="840" y="198" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#4B5563">ppm</text>
  <text x="840" y="224" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#4B5563">Pre-industrial baseline (~1750)</text>
  <text x="840" y="240" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#4B5563">Stable for thousands of years</text>
  <text x="840" y="302" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#9CA3AF">Natural variations never exceeded this level in recorded history</text>

  <!-- Acceleration comparison card (far right) -->
  <rect x="1040" y="122" width="200" height="190" rx="8" fill="#7C3AED" fill-opacity="0.1"/>
  <rect x="1040" y="122" width="200" height="5" rx="2" fill="#7C3AED"/>
  <text x="1140" y="160" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#7C3AED">NATURAL RATE</text>
  <text x="1140" y="186" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#7C3AED">1.5×</text>
  <text x="1140" y="208" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#4B5563">faster than last</text>
  <text x="1140" y="224" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#4B5563">ice age transition</text>
  <text x="1140" y="254" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#9CA3AF">Ice age took</text>
  <text x="1140" y="268" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#9CA3AF">thousands of years</text>
  <text x="1140" y="298" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#9CA3AF">This: ~200 years</text>

  <!-- Three annotation bullets -->
  <text x="40" y="345" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E40AF">Key Context</text>
  <rect x="40" y="352" width="1200" height="1" fill="#E5E7EB"/>

  <!-- Bullet 1 -->
  <rect x="40" y="366" width="380" height="86" rx="6" fill="#EFF6FF"/>
  <use data-icon="circle-exclamation" x="52" y="374" width="18" height="18" fill="#1E40AF"/>
  <text x="80" y="390" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E40AF">Rate of Change Is Unprecedented</text>
  <text x="52" y="410" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">At least 1.5× faster than the natural CO₂</text>
  <text x="52" y="428" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">increase observed at the end of the last</text>
  <text x="52" y="446" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">ice age 20,000 years ago.</text>

  <!-- Bullet 2 -->
  <rect x="440" y="366" width="380" height="86" rx="6" fill="#FFF7ED"/>
  <use data-icon="chart-line" x="452" y="374" width="18" height="18" fill="#EA580C"/>
  <text x="480" y="390" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#EA580C">Continuous Monitoring Since 1958</text>
  <text x="452" y="410" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">NOAA's Mauna Loa Observatory has tracked</text>
  <text x="452" y="428" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">atmospheric CO₂ since 1958 (the Keeling</text>
  <text x="452" y="446" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">Curve). The trend shows no sign of reversal.</text>

  <!-- Bullet 3 -->
  <rect x="840" y="366" width="400" height="86" rx="6" fill="#F0FDF4"/>
  <use data-icon="globe" x="852" y="374" width="18" height="18" fill="#16A34A"/>
  <text x="880" y="390" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#16A34A">Fossil Fuels Are the Primary Driver</text>
  <text x="852" y="410" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">Ground-based and satellite measurements</text>
  <text x="852" y="428" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">confirm the sharp acceleration is linked</text>
  <text x="852" y="446" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">primarily to coal, oil, and natural gas.</text>

  <!-- Simple timeline bar -->
  <text x="40" y="490" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#4B5563">CO₂ TRAJECTORY OVERVIEW</text>
  <rect x="40" y="500" width="1200" height="8" rx="4" fill="#E5E7EB"/>
  <!-- Fill portions -->
  <rect x="40" y="500" width="100" height="8" rx="4" fill="#4B5563"/>
  <!-- from 1750 to ~1850 approx 8% rise -->
  <rect x="140" y="500" width="200" height="8" rx="4" fill="#1E40AF" fill-opacity="0.5"/>
  <rect x="340" y="500" width="400" height="8" rx="4" fill="#1E40AF"/>
  <rect x="740" y="500" width="500" height="8" rx="4" fill="#DC2626"/>
  <!-- Timeline labels -->
  <text x="40" y="524" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#9CA3AF">1750</text>
  <text x="140" y="524" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#9CA3AF">1800</text>
  <text x="240" y="524" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#9CA3AF">1850</text>
  <text x="340" y="524" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#9CA3AF">1900</text>
  <text x="540" y="524" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#9CA3AF">1950</text>
  <text x="740" y="524" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#9CA3AF">1980</text>
  <text x="1040" y="524" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#9CA3AF">2000</text>
  <text x="1200" y="524" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#DC2626" font-weight="bold">2026</text>
  <!-- 429 ppm marker -->
  <line x1="1240" y1="496" x2="1240" y2="512" stroke="#DC2626" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="1240" y="492" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" font-weight="bold" fill="#DC2626">429 ppm</text>

  <!-- Key implication -->
  <rect x="40" y="545" width="1200" height="50" rx="4" fill="#F3F4F6"/>
  <text x="52" y="566" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#111827">Strategic Implication:</text>
  <text x="200" y="566" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">Current CO₂ levels are irreversible on human timescales. Every year of delayed action increases the</text>
  <text x="52" y="584" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">atmospheric burden permanently. This is the scientific backdrop for all current climate negotiations.</text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <rect x="0" y="660" width="1280" height="60" fill="#F9FAFB"/>
  <rect x="0" y="660" width="1280" height="1" fill="#E5E7EB"/>
  <text x="40" y="686" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#9CA3AF">Source: NOAA Mauna Loa Observatory, February 2026 | NASA Vital Signs</text>
  <text x="640" y="686" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#D4AF37" letter-spacing="2">CONFIDENTIAL</text>
  <text x="1240" y="686" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#9CA3AF">2 / 9</text>
</svg>

  <text x="60" y="370" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#9CA3AF" transform="rotate(-90 60 370)">Billion tonnes CO₂</text>

  <!-- Chart plot area: x=90..750, y=170..590. Y range: 0-40 Bt -->

  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="topBar" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">

      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#7C3AED"/>

  <!-- White background -->
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="5" fill="url(#topBar)"/>

  <!-- Page title -->

  <!-- Exhibit takeaway bar -->
  <rect x="40" y="58" width="1200" height="50" rx="2" fill="#111827"/>
  <rect x="40" y="58" width="4" height="50" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <text x="56" y="78" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">The geographic center of emissions has fundamentally shifted: from Europe + North America (>90% in 1900) to Asia (~50%</text>
  <text x="56" y="98" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">today). Africa and South America each contribute only 3–4% — comparable to international aviation and shipping.</text>

  <!-- ===== STACKED BAR COMPARISON ===== -->
  <!-- Two bars: 1900 (left) and 2024 (right), height 400px -->
  <!-- Bar dimensions: width=160, height=400, plot area y=135..595 -->

  <!-- 1900 bar label -->
  <text x="215" y="130" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#374151">1900</text>
  <text x="215" y="148" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#9CA3AF">Total: ~2 Bt/yr</text>

  <!-- 1900 stacked bar (x=135..295, y=155..585, height=430) -->
  <!-- Europe+US: >90% = 387px high, top = 155+43=198, rest below -->
  <!-- Rest of World: ~10% = 43px -->
  <!-- Draw from bottom: RoW at bottom, then EU+US on top -->
  <!-- Rest of World (gray) -->
  <rect x="135" y="542" width="160" height="43" fill="#9CA3AF"/>
  <text x="215" y="567" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#FFFFFF">RoW ~10%</text>

  <!-- Europe + US (dark blue, dominant) -->
  <rect x="135" y="155" width="160" height="387" fill="#1E40AF"/>
  <text x="215" y="300" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Europe</text>
  <text x="215" y="320" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">+ US</text>
  <text x="215" y="348" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">>90%</text>
  <text x="215" y="372" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#BFDBFE">of global total</text>

  <!-- Bracket indicating 1900 bar height -->
  <line x1="305" y1="155" x2="305" y2="585" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4,3"/>

  <!-- 2024 bar label -->
  <text x="555" y="130" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#374151">2024</text>
  <text x="555" y="148" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#9CA3AF">Total: ~35+ Bt/yr</text>

  <!-- 2024 stacked bar (x=475..635, y=155..585, height=430) -->
  <!-- Breakdown (from top to bottom):
    Asia: ~50% = 215px  → y=155, h=215
    US: ~14% = 60px → y=370, h=60
    Europe/EU: ~7% = 30px → y=430, h=30
    Latin Am: ~4% = 17px → y=460, h=17
    Africa: ~3% = 13px → y=477, h=13
    Other: ~22% = 95px → y=490, h=95
  -->
  <!-- Asia (red-orange, dominant now) -->
  <rect x="475" y="155" width="160" height="215" fill="#DC2626"/>
  <text x="555" y="238" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Asia</text>
  <text x="555" y="262" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">~50%</text>
  <text x="555" y="284" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#FECACA">incl. China, India, SE Asia</text>

  <!-- US (blue) -->
  <rect x="475" y="370" width="160" height="60" fill="#1E40AF"/>
  <text x="555" y="404" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">US ~14%</text>

  <!-- Europe (purple) -->
  <rect x="475" y="430" width="160" height="30" fill="#6366F1"/>
  <text x="555" y="449" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#FFFFFF">EU ~7%</text>

  <!-- Latin America (green) -->
  <rect x="475" y="460" width="160" height="17" fill="#16A34A"/>
  <text x="555" y="472" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="9" fill="#FFFFFF">LatAm ~4%</text>

  <!-- Africa (orange) -->
  <rect x="475" y="477" width="160" height="13" fill="#EA580C"/>
  <text x="555" y="488" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="9" fill="#FFFFFF">Africa ~3%</text>

  <!-- Other (gray) -->
  <rect x="475" y="490" width="160" height="95" fill="#9CA3AF"/>
  <text x="555" y="540" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#FFFFFF">Other ~22%</text>

  <!-- Arrow showing shift -->
  <polygon points="330,360 350,350 350,370" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <line x1="315" y1="360" x2="350" y2="360" stroke="#D4AF37" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="340" y="348" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#D4AF37">SHIFT</text>

  <!-- Vertical divider for callout section -->
  <line x1="680" y1="122" x2="680" y2="650" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>

  <!-- ===== RIGHT: Key Callout Cards ===== -->
  <!-- Card 1: Asia -->
  <rect x="710" y="130" width="530" height="100" rx="6" fill="#FEF2F2"/>
  <rect x="710" y="130" width="5" height="100" rx="3" fill="#DC2626"/>
  <text x="725" y="158" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#DC2626">~50%</text>
  <text x="825" y="158" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#111827">Asia (2024)</text>
  <text x="725" y="178" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">China (~27%), India (~8%), and the rest of Asia</text>
  <text x="725" y="196" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">now produce roughly half of all global CO₂ emissions.</text>
  <text x="725" y="218" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#9CA3AF">vs. ≪10% in 1900</text>

  <!-- Card 2: US + Europe -->
  <rect x="710" y="248" width="530" height="100" rx="6" fill="#EFF6FF"/>
  <rect x="710" y="248" width="5" height="100" rx="3" fill="#1E40AF"/>
  <text x="725" y="276" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E40AF"><33%</text>
  <text x="825" y="276" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#111827">US + Europe (2024)</text>
  <text x="725" y="296" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">US (~14%) + EU (~7%) = less than one-third of</text>
  <text x="725" y="314" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">global emissions. Still declining, but slowly.</text>
  <text x="725" y="336" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#9CA3AF">vs. >90% combined in 1900</text>

  <!-- Card 3: Africa + LatAm -->
  <rect x="710" y="366" width="530" height="100" rx="6" fill="#F0FDF4"/>
  <rect x="710" y="366" width="5" height="100" rx="3" fill="#16A34A"/>
  <text x="725" y="394" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#16A34A">3–4%</text>
  <text x="825" y="394" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#111827">Africa + South America Each</text>
  <text x="725" y="414" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">Each region contributes just 3–4% of global</text>
  <text x="725" y="432" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">emissions — comparable to international aviation</text>
  <text x="725" y="450" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">and shipping combined.</text>

  <!-- Population context card -->
  <rect x="710" y="484" width="530" height="60" rx="6" fill="#F5F3FF"/>
  <rect x="710" y="484" width="5" height="60" rx="3" fill="#7C3AED"/>
  <use data-icon="users" x="722" y="494" width="16" height="16" fill="#7C3AED"/>
  <text x="748" y="507" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#7C3AED">Population Context:</text>
  <text x="748" y="527" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">Asia is home to ~60% of the world's population yet produces ~50% of emissions — closer to</text>
  <text x="748" y="524" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151"> </text>
  <text x="748" y="537" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">proportional parity than the historical 1900 picture where Europe+US used 90% on 25% of people.</text>

  <!-- Scale legend -->
  <text x="40" y="610" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#6B7280">LEGEND:</text>
  <rect x="90" y="600" width="14" height="14" fill="#1E40AF"/>
  <text x="110" y="612" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#374151">Europe + US</text>
  <rect x="210" y="600" width="14" height="14" fill="#DC2626"/>
  <text x="230" y="612" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#374151">Asia</text>
  <rect x="280" y="600" width="14" height="14" fill="#6366F1"/>
  <text x="300" y="612" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#374151">EU</text>
  <rect x="330" y="600" width="14" height="14" fill="#16A34A"/>
  <text x="350" y="612" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#374151">Latin America</text>
  <rect x="450" y="600" width="14" height="14" fill="#EA580C"/>
  <text x="470" y="612" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#374151">Africa</text>
  <rect x="520" y="600" width="14" height="14" fill="#9CA3AF"/>
  <text x="540" y="612" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#374151">Other</text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <rect x="0" y="660" width="1280" height="60" fill="#F9FAFB"/>
  <rect x="0" y="660" width="1280" height="1" fill="#E5E7EB"/>
  <text x="40" y="686" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#9CA3AF">Source: Global Carbon Budget 2025; Our World in Data — CO₂ and Greenhouse Gas Emissions</text>
  <text x="640" y="686" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#D4AF37" letter-spacing="2">CONFIDENTIAL</text>
  <text x="1240" y="686" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#9CA3AF">5 / 9</text>
</svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720" width="1280" height="720">
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="topBar" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#1E40AF"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#7C3AED"/>
    </linearGradient>

  <!-- White background -->
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="5" fill="url(#topBar)"/>

  <!-- Page title -->

  <!-- Exhibit takeaway bar -->
  <rect x="40" y="58" width="1200" height="50" rx="2" fill="#111827"/>
  <rect x="40" y="58" width="4" height="50" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <text x="56" y="78" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">The geographic center of emissions has fundamentally shifted: from Europe + North America (>90% in 1900) to Asia (~50%</text>
  <text x="56" y="98" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">today). Africa and South America each contribute only 3–4% — comparable to international aviation and shipping.</text>

  <!-- ===== STACKED BAR COMPARISON ===== -->
  <!-- Two bars: 1900 (left) and 2024 (right), height 400px -->
  <!-- Bar dimensions: width=160, height=400, plot area y=135..595 -->

  <!-- 1900 bar label -->
  <text x="215" y="130" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#374151">1900</text>
  <text x="215" y="148" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#9CA3AF">Total: ~2 Bt/yr</text>

  <!-- 1900 stacked bar (x=135..295, y=155..585, height=430) -->
  <!-- Europe+US: >90% = 387px high, top = 155+43=198, rest below -->
  <!-- Rest of World: ~10% = 43px -->
  <!-- Draw from bottom: RoW at bottom, then EU+US on top -->
  <!-- Rest of World (gray) -->
  <rect x="135" y="542" width="160" height="43" fill="#9CA3AF"/>
  <text x="215" y="567" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#FFFFFF">RoW ~10%</text>

  <!-- Europe + US (dark blue, dominant) -->
  <rect x="135" y="155" width="160" height="387" fill="#1E40AF"/>
  <text x="215" y="300" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Europe</text>
  <text x="215" y="320" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">+ US</text>
  <text x="215" y="348" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">>90%</text>
  <text x="215" y="372" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#BFDBFE">of global total</text>

  <!-- Bracket indicating 1900 bar height -->
  <line x1="305" y1="155" x2="305" y2="585" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4,3"/>

  <!-- 2024 bar label -->
  <text x="555" y="130" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#374151">2024</text>
  <text x="555" y="148" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#9CA3AF">Total: ~35+ Bt/yr</text>

  <!-- 2024 stacked bar (x=475..635, y=155..585, height=430) -->
  <!-- Breakdown (from top to bottom):
    Asia: ~50% = 215px  → y=155, h=215
    US: ~14% = 60px → y=370, h=60
    Europe/EU: ~7% = 30px → y=430, h=30
    Latin Am: ~4% = 17px → y=460, h=17
    Africa: ~3% = 13px → y=477, h=13
    Other: ~22% = 95px → y=490, h=95
  -->
