  <rect x="475" y="155" width="160" height="215" fill="#DC2626"/>
  <text x="555" y="238" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Asia</text>
  <text x="555" y="262" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">~50%</text>
  <text x="555" y="284" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#FECACA">incl. China, India, SE Asia</text>

  <!-- US (blue) -->
  <rect x="475" y="370" width="160" height="60" fill="#1E40AF"/>
  <text x="555" y="404" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">US ~14%</text>

  <!-- Europe (purple) -->
  <rect x="475" y="430" width="160" height="30" fill="#6366F1"/>
  <text x="555" y="449" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#FFFFFF">EU ~7%</text>

  <!-- Latin America (green) -->
  <rect x="475" y="460" width="160" height="17" fill="#16A34A"/>
  <text x="555" y="472" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="9" fill="#FFFFFF">LatAm ~4%</text>

  <!-- Africa (orange) -->
  <rect x="475" y="477" width="160" height="13" fill="#EA580C"/>
  <text x="555" y="488" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="9" fill="#FFFFFF">Africa ~3%</text>

  <!-- Other (gray) -->
  <rect x="475" y="490" width="160" height="95" fill="#9CA3AF"/>
  <text x="555" y="540" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#FFFFFF">Other ~22%</text>

  <line x1="315" y1="360" x2="350" y2="360" stroke="#D4AF37" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="340" y="348" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#D4AF37">SHIFT</text>

  <!-- Vertical divider for callout section -->
  <line x1="680" y1="122" x2="680" y2="650" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>

  <!-- ===== RIGHT: Key Callout Cards ===== -->
  <!-- Card 1: Asia -->
  <rect x="710" y="130" width="530" height="100" rx="6" fill="#FEF2F2"/>
  <rect x="710" y="130" width="5" height="100" rx="3" fill="#DC2626"/>
  <text x="725" y="158" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#DC2626">~50%</text>
  <text x="825" y="158" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#111827">Asia (2024)</text>
  <text x="725" y="178" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">China (~27%), India (~8%), and the rest of Asia</text>
  <text x="725" y="196" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">now produce roughly half of all global CO₂ emissions.</text>
  <text x="725" y="218" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#9CA3AF">vs. ≪10% in 1900</text>

  <!-- Card 2: US + Europe -->
  <rect x="710" y="248" width="530" height="100" rx="6" fill="#EFF6FF"/>
  <rect x="710" y="248" width="5" height="100" rx="3" fill="#1E40AF"/>
  <text x="725" y="276" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E40AF"><33%</text>
  <text x="825" y="276" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#111827">US + Europe (2024)</text>
  <text x="725" y="296" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">US (~14%) + EU (~7%) = less than one-third of</text>
  <text x="725" y="314" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">global emissions. Still declining, but slowly.</text>
  <text x="725" y="336" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#9CA3AF">vs. >90% combined in 1900</text>

  <!-- Card 3: Africa + LatAm -->
  <rect x="710" y="366" width="530" height="100" rx="6" fill="#F0FDF4"/>
  <rect x="710" y="366" width="5" height="100" rx="3" fill="#16A34A"/>
  <text x="725" y="394" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#16A34A">3–4%</text>
  <text x="825" y="394" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#111827">Africa + South America Each</text>
  <text x="725" y="414" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">Each region contributes just 3–4% of global</text>
  <text x="725" y="432" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">emissions — comparable to international aviation</text>
  <text x="725" y="450" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">and shipping combined.</text>

  <!-- Population context card -->
  <rect x="710" y="484" width="530" height="60" rx="6" fill="#F5F3FF"/>
  <rect x="710" y="484" width="5" height="60" rx="3" fill="#7C3AED"/>
  <use data-icon="users" x="722" y="494" width="16" height="16" fill="#7C3AED"/>
  <text x="748" y="507" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#7C3AED">Population Context:</text>
  <text x="748" y="527" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">Asia is home to ~60% of the world's population yet produces ~50% of emissions — closer to</text>
  <text x="748" y="524" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151"> </text>
  <text x="748" y="537" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#374151">proportional parity than the historical 1900 picture where Europe+US used 90% on 25% of people.</text>

  <!-- Scale legend -->
  <text x="40" y="610" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#6B7280">LEGEND:</text>
  <rect x="90" y="600" width="14" height="14" fill="#1E40AF"/>

  <text x="230" y="612" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#374151">Asia</text>
  <rect x="280" y="600" width="14" height="14" fill="#6366F1"/>
  <text x="300" y="612" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#374151">EU</text>
  <rect x="330" y="600" width="14" height="14" fill="#16A34A"/>
  <text x="350" y="612" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#374151">Latin America</text>
  <rect x="450" y="600" width="14" height="14" fill="#EA580C"/>
  <text x="470" y="612" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#374151">Africa</text>
  <rect x="520" y="600" width="14" height="14" fill="#9CA3AF"/>
  <text x="540" y="612" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#374151">Other</text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <rect x="0" y="660" width="1280" height="60" fill="#F9FAFB"/>
  <rect x="0" y="660" width="1280" height="1" fill="#E5E7EB"/>
  <text x="40" y="686" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#9CA3AF">Source: Global Carbon Budget 2025; Our World in Data — CO₂ and Greenhouse Gas Emissions</text>
  <text x="640" y="686" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#D4AF37" letter-spacing="2">CONFIDENTIAL</text>
  <text x="1240" y="686" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#9CA3AF">5 / 9</text>
</svg>

  <rect x="40" y="58" width="4" height="50" fill="#D4AF37"/>

  <text x="56" y="98" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Southeast Asia, and parts of Africa are increasing (+2% to +10% or more).</text>

  <!-- Main map image — full width panel -->
  <rect x="40" y="118" width="1200" height="420" rx="4" fill="#F3F4F6"/>
  <image href="../images/figure_4.jpg" x="40" y="118" width="1200" height="420" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/>

  <!-- Semi-transparent overlay boxes for callout annotations -->

  <rect x="60" y="138" width="220" height="60" rx="6" fill="#1E40AF" fill-opacity="0.88"/>
  <text x="170" y="162" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">US & EU</text>
  <text x="170" y="180" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#BFDBFE">−1% to −5%</text>
  <text x="170" y="194" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#93C5FD">Declining trajectory</text>

  <!-- Russia annotation -->
  <rect x="700" y="138" width="220" height="60" rx="6" fill="#DC2626" fill-opacity="0.88"/>
  <text x="810" y="162" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Russia + SE Asia</text>
  <text x="810" y="180" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#FECACA">+2% to +10%+</text>
  <text x="810" y="194" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#FCA5A5">Significant increases</text>

  <!-- South America annotation -->
  <rect x="280" y="380" width="200" height="50" rx="6" fill="#EA580C" fill-opacity="0.88"/>
  <text x="380" y="402" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">S. America</text>
  <text x="380" y="420" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#FFEDD5">Some >10% increases</text>

  <text x="52" y="578" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#374151">2024 Change Legend:</text>

  <!-- Legend items -->
  <rect x="188" y="566" width="22" height="16" rx="2" fill="#1E3A8A"/>
  <text x="216" y="579" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#374151">−5%+ (US, N. Europe)</text>

  <rect x="390" y="566" width="22" height="16" rx="2" fill="#3B82F6"/>
  <text x="418" y="579" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#374151">−1% to −4%</text>

  <rect x="540" y="566" width="22" height="16" rx="2" fill="#D1D5DB"/>
  <text x="568" y="579" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#374151">Roughly stable</text>

  <rect x="690" y="566" width="22" height="16" rx="2" fill="#F97316"/>
  <text x="718" y="579" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#374151">+2% to +5%</text>

  <rect x="830" y="566" width="22" height="16" rx="2" fill="#DC2626"/>
  <text x="858" y="579" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#374151">+5% to +10%+</text>

  <!-- Second legend row -->
  <text x="188" y="600" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#374151">Blue tones = declining; Orange/Red = increasing; Size reflects absolute emission level</text>

  <!-- Key regional summary row -->
  <rect x="40" y="615" width="1200" height="34" rx="4" fill="#111827"/>
  <text x="52" y="628" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#60A5FA">US & EU:</text>
  <text x="100" y="628" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#D1D5DB">−1% to −5%  |</text>
  <text x="210" y="628" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#FCA5A5">Russia:</text>
  <text x="256" y="628" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#D1D5DB">+2% to +5%  |</text>
  <text x="370" y="628" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#FCA5A5">SE Asia:</text>
  <text x="420" y="628" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#D1D5DB">+2% to +10%  |</text>
  <text x="545" y="628" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#FCA5A5">Parts of Africa:</text>
  <text x="660" y="628" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#D1D5DB">+2% to +10%  |</text>
  <text x="775" y="628" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#FCA5A5">S. America (some):</text>
  <text x="910" y="628" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#D1D5DB">>10% increase</text>
  <text x="52" y="644" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#9CA3AF">Global net: Emissions still rising (no year-on-year peak yet) — declines in rich countries offset by growth elsewhere</text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <rect x="0" y="660" width="1280" height="60" fill="#F9FAFB"/>
  <rect x="0" y="660" width="1280" height="1" fill="#E5E7EB"/>
  <text x="40" y="686" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#9CA3AF">Source: Global Carbon Budget 2025; Our World in Data — CO₂ and Greenhouse Gas Emissions</text>
  <text x="640" y="686" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#D4AF37" letter-spacing="2">CONFIDENTIAL</text>
  <text x="1240" y="686" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#9CA3AF">7 / 9</text>
</svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720" width="1280" height="720">
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="topBar" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#1E40AF"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#7C3AED"/>
    </linearGradient>
  </defs>

  <!-- White background -->
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="5" fill="url(#topBar)"/>

  <!-- Page title -->
  <text x="40" y="46" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#111827">Energy Mix Explains Why France Emits Far Less Per Capita Than Germany</text>

  <!-- Exhibit takeaway bar -->
  <rect x="40" y="58" width="1200" height="50" rx="2" fill="#111827"/>
  <rect x="40" y="58" width="4" height="50" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <text x="56" y="78" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Countries at similar prosperity levels can have dramatically different per capita emissions. Energy mix — especially the</text>
  <text x="56" y="98" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">share of nuclear and renewables vs. fossil fuels — is the key differentiator, not GDP alone.</text>

  <!-- ===== LEFT PANEL: Two contrast cards ===== -->
  <!-- Card A: France/UK (low emitters) -->
  <rect x="40" y="122" width="560" height="220" rx="8" fill="#EFF6FF"/>
  <rect x="40" y="122" width="6" height="220" rx="3" fill="#1E40AF"/>

  <!-- Flag-style header -->
  <rect x="46" y="122" width="554" height="44" rx="4" fill="#1E40AF"/>
  <text x="326" y="150" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">France & United Kingdom</text>

  <text x="60" y="186" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="40" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E40AF">~4 t</text>
  <text x="175" y="186" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#374151">per person per year</text>

  <text x="60" y="212" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">● High nuclear share (France: ~70% of electricity)</text>
  <text x="60" y="230" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">● Growing renewable energy portfolio</text>
  <text x="60" y="248" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">● Relatively low coal and gas dependence</text>
  <text x="60" y="266" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">● Similar GDP per capita to Germany/Netherlands</text>

  <rect x="60" y="280" width="240" height="28" rx="6" fill="#1E40AF"/>
  <text x="180" y="299" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Below world average (5 t)</text>

  <!-- Card B: Germany/Netherlands (higher emitters) -->
  <rect x="40" y="362" width="560" height="210" rx="8" fill="#FFF7ED"/>
  <rect x="40" y="362" width="6" height="210" rx="3" fill="#EA580C"/>

  <!-- Flag-style header -->
  <rect x="46" y="362" width="554" height="44" rx="4" fill="#EA580C"/>
  <text x="326" y="390" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Germany & Netherlands</text>

  <text x="60" y="426" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="40" font-weight="bold" fill="#EA580C">~7–8 t</text>
  <text x="220" y="426" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#374151">per person per year</text>

  <text x="60" y="452" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">● Germany phased out nuclear (post-Fukushima)</text>
  <text x="60" y="470" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">● Higher reliance on natural gas and coal</text>
  <text x="60" y="488" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">● Netherlands: significant gas infrastructure</text>
  <text x="60" y="506" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">● Renewables growing but fossil still dominant</text>

  <rect x="60" y="518" width="260" height="28" rx="6" fill="#EA580C"/>
  <text x="190" y="537" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Nearly double France/UK per capita</text>

  <!-- Divider VS element -->
  <text x="40" y="356" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="26" font-weight="bold" fill="#111827">VS</text>

  <!-- ===== RIGHT PANEL: Comparison table ===== -->
  <rect x="630" y="122" width="610" height="455" rx="6" fill="#F9FAFB"/>

  <!-- Table header -->
  <rect x="630" y="122" width="610" height="44" rx="4" fill="#111827"/>
  <text x="935" y="150" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Energy Mix & Per Capita CO₂ Comparison</text>

  <!-- Column headers -->
  <rect x="630" y="166" width="610" height="32" fill="#1F2937"/>
  <text x="730" y="187" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#9CA3AF">Country</text>
  <text x="835" y="187" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#9CA3AF">CO₂/person</text>
  <text x="940" y="187" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#9CA3AF">Nuclear</text>
  <text x="1050" y="187" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#9CA3AF">Renewable</text>
  <text x="1165" y="187" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#9CA3AF">Fossil Reliance</text>

  <!-- Row 1: France -->
  <rect x="630" y="198" width="610" height="52" fill="#EFF6FF"/>
  <rect x="630" y="198" width="4" height="52" fill="#1E40AF"/>

  <text x="1050" y="229" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Moderate</text>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720" width="1280" height="720">
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="topBar" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#1E40AF"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#7C3AED"/>
    </linearGradient>
  </defs>

  <!-- White background -->
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="5" fill="url(#topBar)"/>

  <!-- Page title -->
  <text x="40" y="46" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#111827">Key Takeaways: Emissions Still Rising, But the Map of Responsibility Is Shifting</text>

  <!-- Exhibit takeaway bar -->
  <rect x="40" y="58" width="1200" height="50" rx="2" fill="#111827"/>
  <rect x="40" y="58" width="4" height="50" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <text x="56" y="78" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Five facts every climate negotiator needs: emissions are still rising, but who is responsible — historically and per capita —</text>
  <text x="56" y="98" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">is more nuanced than total tonnage alone.</text>

  <!-- ===== 5 Takeaway Cards in 3+2 grid ===== -->
  <!-- Row 1: 3 cards (x=40,440,840 width=380, h=200) -->
  <!-- Row 2: 2 cards (x=140,660, width=420, h=170) centred -->

  <!-- Card 1: 35+ Bt -->
  <rect x="40" y="122" width="378" height="205" rx="8" fill="#FEF2F2"/>
  <rect x="40" y="122" width="378" height="5" rx="2" fill="#DC2626"/>
  <!-- Number badge -->
  <circle cx="74" cy="153" r="18" fill="#DC2626"/>
  <text x="74" y="158" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">1</text>
  <text x="100" y="153" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#DC2626">35+ Billion Tonnes</text>
  <text x="100" y="170" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#DC2626">and Still Climbing</text>
  <line x1="56" y1="178" x2="402" y2="178" stroke="#FECACA" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="56" y="198" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">Global annual CO₂ emissions have</text>
  <text x="56" y="216" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">not yet peaked. Growth is slowing</text>
  <text x="56" y="234" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">but absolute levels continue to rise,</text>
  <text x="56" y="252" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">driven by Asia and other regions.</text>
  <text x="56" y="315" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#9CA3AF">Source: Global Carbon Budget 2025</text>

  <!-- Card 2: China/India -->
  <rect x="438" y="122" width="378" height="205" rx="8" fill="#FFF7ED"/>
  <rect x="438" y="122" width="378" height="5" rx="2" fill="#EA580C"/>
  <circle cx="472" cy="153" r="18" fill="#EA580C"/>
  <text x="472" y="158" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">2</text>
  <text x="498" y="153" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#EA580C">China Leads at 27%,</text>
  <text x="498" y="170" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#EA580C">India Rising Fast</text>
  <line x1="454" y1="178" x2="800" y2="178" stroke="#FED7AA" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="454" y="198" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">China emits ~12.5 Bt (~27% of global</text>
  <text x="454" y="216" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">total). India (~3 Bt, ~8%) is the third-</text>
  <text x="454" y="234" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">largest emitter, growing rapidly, and</text>
  <text x="454" y="252" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">has surpassed the entire EU-27.</text>
  <text x="454" y="315" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#9CA3AF">Source: Global Carbon Budget 2025</text>

  <!-- Card 3: 150x inequality -->
  <rect x="836" y="122" width="404" height="205" rx="8" fill="#F5F3FF"/>
  <rect x="836" y="122" width="404" height="5" rx="2" fill="#7C3AED"/>
  <circle cx="870" cy="153" r="18" fill="#7C3AED"/>
  <text x="870" y="158" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">3</text>
  <text x="896" y="153" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#7C3AED">150× Per Capita</text>
  <text x="896" y="170" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#7C3AED">Inequality</text>
  <line x1="852" y1="178" x2="1234" y2="178" stroke="#DDD6FE" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="852" y="198" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">US: ~15 t/person vs. Chad: ~0.1 t.</text>
  <text x="852" y="216" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">The average American emits in under</text>
  <text x="852" y="234" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">two days what the average Chadian</text>
  <text x="852" y="252" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">emits in an entire year.</text>
  <text x="852" y="315" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#9CA3AF">Source: Global Carbon Budget 2025</text>

  <!-- Row 2: 2 wider cards centered -->
  <!-- Card 4: US/Europe declining -->
  <rect x="140" y="347" width="440" height="185" rx="8" fill="#EFF6FF"/>
  <rect x="140" y="347" width="440" height="5" rx="2" fill="#1E40AF"/>
  <circle cx="178" cy="378" r="18" fill="#1E40AF"/>
  <text x="178" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">4</text>
  <text x="204" y="378" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E40AF">US and Europe Are Declining,</text>
  <text x="204" y="395" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E40AF">But Historical Responsibility Remains</text>
  <line x1="156" y1="405" x2="574" y2="405" stroke="#BFDBFE" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="156" y="425" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">US emissions are down ~−1% to −5% in 2024; EU</text>
  <text x="156" y="443" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">similarly. But cumulative historical emissions from</text>
  <text x="156" y="461" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">industrialized nations remain large — a key point</text>
  <text x="156" y="479" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">in loss-and-damage and finance negotiations.</text>
  <text x="156" y="522" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#9CA3AF">Source: Global Carbon Budget 2025</text>

  <!-- Card 5: Energy mix / policy lever -->
  <rect x="700" y="347" width="440" height="185" rx="8" fill="#F0FDF4"/>
  <rect x="700" y="347" width="440" height="5" rx="2" fill="#16A34A"/>
  <circle cx="738" cy="378" r="18" fill="#16A34A"/>
  <text x="738" y="383" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">5</text>
  <text x="764" y="378" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#16A34A">Energy Mix Is the</text>
  <text x="764" y="395" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#16A34A">Critical Policy Lever</text>
  <line x1="716" y1="405" x2="1134" y2="405" stroke="#BBF7D0" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="716" y="425" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">France (~4 t) vs. Germany (~7 t): comparable</text>
  <text x="716" y="443" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">GDP, dramatically different emissions. Nuclear</text>
  <text x="716" y="461" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">and renewables — not prosperity alone —</text>
  <text x="716" y="479" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#374151">determine per capita outcomes.</text>

arguments.content:
# 01_cover

Welcome. Over the next twenty minutes, we'll walk through the most critical data on global CO₂ emissions — from the Industrial Revolution through 2024 — examining not just who emits the most in total, but how the geography of emissions has shifted, and what the stark per capita inequalities mean for how we structure climate agreements. [Pause]

This analysis is grounded entirely in the Global Carbon Budget 2025, NOAA's Mauna Loa Observatory data, and Our World in Data.

Key points: ① Historical scope 1750–2024 ② Audience: policy analysts and climate negotiators ③ Three analytical lenses: totals, regional shares, per capita equity
Duration: 1 minute

---

# 02_atmospheric_co2

[Transition] Before we look at who emits what, let's establish the atmospheric reality that drives this conversation.

As of February 2026, NOAA's Mauna Loa Observatory records atmospheric CO₂ at 429 parts per million. [Data] That's 429 ppm — against a pre-industrial baseline of roughly 280 ppm. A 53% increase. [Pause]

What's striking is not just the magnitude, but the speed. [Benchmark] The natural increase observed at the end of the last ice age 20,000 years ago — a roughly comparable magnitude of CO₂ change — took thousands of years. This has occurred in approximately 200 years. The Keeling Curve, measured continuously since 1958, shows no sign of reversal.

[Scan Room] The strategic implication for negotiators is simple: every year of inaction adds permanently to this atmospheric stock.

Key points: ① 429 ppm current (Feb 2026) ② 53% above pre-industrial 280 ppm baseline ③ Rate of change is at least 1.5× faster than natural ice-age transitions
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 03_global_trajectory

[Transition] Now let's look at how we got here — the trajectory of total global emissions since the Industrial Revolution.

The chart on the left tells a stark story. Before 1900, emissions were negligible on a global scale. [Data] By 1950, the world was emitting roughly 6 billion tonnes per year. By 1990, that had nearly quadrupled to around 20 billion tonnes. [Pause]

Today, we exceed 35 billion tonnes annually — a more than six-fold increase from 1950, in just 74 years. Growth has slowed in recent years, but we have not yet seen a peak. [Scan Room] To be clear: slower growth is not the same as declining. Absolute emissions are still rising each year.

Key points: ① 1950 baseline: 6 Bt ② 1990 (Kyoto reference year): ~20 Bt ③ 2024: 35+ Bt and not yet peaked
Duration: 2 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, highlight just the three milestone numbers and move on]

---

# 04_country_totals

[Transition] Knowing the global total, let's now ask: who is responsible?

The picture is dominated by a single country. [Data] China now emits over 12.5 billion tonnes annually — roughly 27% of the global total — more than double the United States at approximately 5 billion tonnes. [Pause]

The US, for its part, has been declining since its peak of around 6 billion tonnes in 2005. The EU-27, at 2.7 billion tonnes, continues to fall. But India — now at approximately 3 billion tonnes — has surpassed the EU-27 and is still growing rapidly. [Benchmark] India is now the world's third-largest emitter, and its trajectory is sharply upward.

[Scan Room] The chart on the right from Our World in Data shows the historical context — China's steep rise post-2000 is unmistakable.

Key points: ① China: ~12.5 Bt (~27% global) ② US: ~5 Bt, declining from 2005 peak ③ India: ~3 Bt, rising, has surpassed EU-27
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 05_regional_shift

[Transition] Looking at individual countries is important, but the regional picture reveals an even more profound structural shift.

In 1900, Europe and the United States together accounted for more than 90% of all global CO₂ emissions. [Pause] Look at the left bar. One color — dark blue — dominates almost entirely.

Now look at 2024. Asia — China, India, and the rest — produces approximately half of all global emissions. The US and Europe combined are below one-third. [Data] Meanwhile, Africa and South America each contribute just 3–4% of global emissions — comparable to international aviation and shipping combined. [Pause]

[Benchmark] Asia is home to roughly 60% of the world's population, so a 50% emissions share actually represents relative parity — a very different picture from 1900 when Europe and the US produced 90% of emissions on roughly 25% of the world's population.

raw_arguments.content:
# 01_cover

Welcome. Over the next twenty minutes, we'll walk through the most critical data on global CO₂ emissions — from the Industrial Revolution through 2024 — examining not just who emits the most in total, but how the geography of emissions has shifted, and what the stark per capita inequalities mean for how we structure climate agreements. [Pause]

This analysis is grounded entirely in the Global Carbon Budget 2025, NOAA's Mauna Loa Observatory data, and Our World in Data.

Key points: ① Historical scope 1750–2024 ② Audience: policy analysts and climate negotiators ③ Three analytical lenses: totals, regional shares, per capita equity
Duration: 1 minute

---

# 02_atmospheric_co2

[Transition] Before we look at who emits what, let's establish the atmospheric reality that drives this conversation.

As of February 2026, NOAA's Mauna Loa Observatory records atmospheric CO₂ at 429 parts per million. [Data] That's 429 ppm — against a pre-industrial baseline of roughly 280 ppm. A 53% increase. [Pause]

What's striking is not just the magnitude, but the speed. [Benchmark] The natural increase observed at the end of the last ice age 20,000 years ago — a roughly comparable magnitude of CO₂ change — took thousands of years. This has occurred in approximately 200 years. The Keeling Curve, measured continuously since 1958, shows no sign of reversal.

[Scan Room] The strategic implication for negotiators is simple: every year of inaction adds permanently to this atmospheric stock.

Key points: ① 429 ppm current (Feb 2026) ② 53% above pre-industrial 280 ppm baseline ③ Rate of change is at least 1.5× faster than natural ice-age transitions
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 03_global_trajectory

[Transition] Now let's look at how we got here — the trajectory of total global emissions since the Industrial Revolution.

The chart on the left tells a stark story. Before 1900, emissions were negligible on a global scale. [Data] By 1950, the world was emitting roughly 6 billion tonnes per year. By 1990, that had nearly quadrupled to around 20 billion tonnes. [Pause]

Today, we exceed 35 billion tonnes annually — a more than six-fold increase from 1950, in just 74 years. Growth has slowed in recent years, but we have not yet seen a peak. [Scan Room] To be clear: slower growth is not the same as declining. Absolute emissions are still rising each year.

Key points: ① 1950 baseline: 6 Bt ② 1990 (Kyoto reference year): ~20 Bt ③ 2024: 35+ Bt and not yet peaked
Duration: 2 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, highlight just the three milestone numbers and move on]

---

# 04_country_totals

[Transition] Knowing the global total, let's now ask: who is responsible?

The picture is dominated by a single country. [Data] China now emits over 12.5 billion tonnes annually — roughly 27% of the global total — more than double the United States at approximately 5 billion tonnes. [Pause]

The US, for its part, has been declining since its peak of around 6 billion tonnes in 2005. The EU-27, at 2.7 billion tonnes, continues to fall. But India — now at approximately 3 billion tonnes — has surpassed the EU-27 and is still growing rapidly. [Benchmark] India is now the world's third-largest emitter, and its trajectory is sharply upward.

[Scan Room] The chart on the right from Our World in Data shows the historical context — China's steep rise post-2000 is unmistakable.

Key points: ① China: ~12.5 Bt (~27% global) ② US: ~5 Bt, declining from 2005 peak ③ India: ~3 Bt, rising, has surpassed EU-27
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 05_regional_shift

[Transition] Looking at individual countries is important, but the regional picture reveals an even more profound structural shift.

In 1900, Europe and the United States together accounted for more than 90% of all global CO₂ emissions. [Pause] Look at the left bar. One color — dark blue — dominates almost entirely.

Now look at 2024. Asia — China, India, and the rest — produces approximately half of all global emissions. The US and Europe combined are below one-third. [Data] Meanwhile, Africa and South America each contribute just 3–4% of global emissions — comparable to international aviation and shipping combined. [Pause]

[Benchmark] Asia is home to roughly 60% of the world's population, so a 50% emissions share actually represents relative parity — a very different picture from 1900 when Europe and the US produced 90% of emissions on roughly 25% of the world's population.

Key points: ① 1900: EU+US >90% ② 2024: Asia ~50%, EU+US <33% ③ Africa + LatAm: only 3-4% each despite large populations
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 06_per_capita

[Transition] Total national emissions tell us who is responsible in aggregate. But per capita emissions tell us something entirely different: they reveal the equity dimension.

The horizontal bar chart before you shows a 150-fold gap. [Data] The average American emits approximately 15 tonnes of CO₂ per year. The average person in Chad or Niger emits roughly 0.1 tonnes. [Pause] That means an American emits in under two days what a Chadian emits in an entire year.

[Benchmark] The world average is 5 tonnes per person. The US and Canada are three times that. India, at 2 tonnes, is below average. Kenya is under 1 tonne.

The per capita chart on the right — the historical line chart — shows how these gaps have evolved over time. Note particularly how France and the UK cluster far below Germany and the Netherlands, despite comparable wealth. We'll examine that in the next slide.

Key points: ① US: ~15 t/person vs. Chad: ~0.1 t = 150× gap ② World average: ~5 t ③ India (~2t) and Africa (<1t) are far below average despite rising total emissions
Duration: 3 minutes
Flex: [The equity framing here is central to loss-and-damage negotiations — emphasize if the audience includes finance delegations]

---

# 07_annual_change_2024

[Transition] We've looked at the historical arc and the structural inequalities. Now let's examine the most recent data: what happened in 2024?

The map shows annual percentage change in CO₂ emissions. Blue means declining. Orange and red mean increasing. [Data] The United States and most of Europe recorded declines of roughly −1% to −5%. The UK and Nordic countries in particular. [Pause]

But look eastward. Russia, parts of Southeast Asia, and several African nations saw increases of +2% to +10% or more. And some countries in South America experienced very large percentage jumps — over 10%. [Benchmark] The net global result? Emissions are still rising. The declines in rich countries are not yet large enough to offset growth elsewhere.

[Scan Room] The strategic implication: we are in a period of divergence. Some economies are bending the curve; many others are not yet on that path.

Key points: ① US and EU: declining (−1% to −5%) ② Russia, SE Asia, parts of Africa: +2% to +10%+ ③ Global net: still rising, no peak year reached
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 08_energy_mix

[Transition] The per capita data raises an obvious question: why do France and Germany — two prosperous European neighbors — have such different per capita emissions?

The answer is energy mix. [Data] France emits approximately 4 tonnes per person per year. Germany emits approximately 7 tonnes. Same continent, similar GDP, but nearly double the per capita CO₂. [Pause]

[Benchmark] France generates roughly 70% of its electricity from nuclear power. Germany phased out its nuclear capacity following Fukushima and has maintained higher reliance on natural gas and coal. Third: the per capita gap of 150× between the US and Chad is not an abstraction — it is the core equity argument in loss-and-damage and climate finance discussions. [Data] The average American's annual footprint is emitted in under 48 hours by the average Chadian.

Fourth: the US and Europe are declining. But historical cumulative responsibility remains a legitimate point of contention in the negotiating room.

Fifth — and this may be the most actionable finding: energy policy, not prosperity, determines per capita outcomes. France at 4 tonnes and Germany at 7 tonnes are the proof case. The path exists. The question is political will.

[Scan Room] I'm happy to go deeper on any of these five points.
